intro: A folk songwriter with To Be Still just out.
story: Alela Diane played Pickathon in 2009 with To Be Still, on Rough Trade, new that year, a record Uncut called a leap from her last. Alela Diane & Wild Divine followed in 2011 and About Farewell in 2013, and Cusp in 2018 drew praise from The Guardian. She came back to Pickathon four more times, and in 2026 released Who's Keeping Time? on Loose, after Looking Glass on naïve in 2022.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 3 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 1, 7:45 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: An East Tennessee banjo player and radio host.
story: Alex Leach, an East Tennessee banjoist and radio host, brought crisp, traditional bluegrass to Pickathon in 2009. He has since fronted The Alex Leach Band, and in November 2026 he played WDVX's Tennessee Shines and Station Birthday Bash at the Bijou Theatre in Knoxville.
sets: Sun Aug 2, 4:30 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A country-blues guitarist with a Grammy nomination.
story: Alvin Youngblood Hart came to Pickathon in 2009 with a catalog that began with Big Mama's Door on OKeh in 1996. His 2002 album Down in the Alley was nominated for the 2003 Grammy for Best Traditional Blues Album, and Living Blues readers voted him top blues guitarist more than once in the early 2000s. He still plays across Europe, with dates in Finland in 2026 and a slot booked at Scotland's Orkney Blues Festival.
sets: Sun Aug 2, 12:30 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 2, 6 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 2, 7:45 pm, Fir Meadow Stage

intro: A Southern California Western swing and rockabilly band.
story: Big Sandy & His Fly-Rite Boys, the Southern California band led by Robert Williams, were Western swing and rockabilly veterans when they played Pickathon in 2009. More than three decades into their career they are still on the road, with club dates in Buffalo and across North America in fall 2026.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 7 pm, Mountain View Stage · Fri Jul 31, 10 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 1, 12:30 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: A Portland band with Furr behind them.
story: Blitzen Trapper, the Portland band led by Eric Earley, played Pickathon in 2009 with Furr, their Sub Pop breakthrough, behind them, and returned in 2012. American Goldwing followed in 2011 and Holy Smokes Future Jokes on Yep Roc in 2020. In 2024 came 100's of 1000's, Millions of Billions, built from old four-track tapes from the 1990s.
sets: Sun Aug 2, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 8:30 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A Michigan trio of whimsical, cello-laced folk.
story: Breathe Owl Breathe, a Michigan trio making whimsical, cello-laced indie folk, played Pickathon in 2009 and returned in 2010, 2011 and 2013. Magic Central came out in 2010 and Passage of Pegasus in 2013. Micah Middaugh and company have kept pairing music with visual art, and a December 2026 winter concert comes with their traveling exhibition Oval Realms.

intro: An Australian singer of 1920s hokum and calypso.
story: C.W. Stoneking, the Australian singer and guitarist, brought 1920s hokum, calypso and New Orleans brass to Pickathon in 2009, with Jungle Blues out and about to win the ARIA Award for Best Blues and Roots Album. He returned in 2016. Gon' Boogaloo won the same ARIA category in 2015, studio albums are rare, and in 2026 he finished a 23-date European tour.

intro: A Michigan folk duo of earnest harmonies.
story: Billed as Daisy May & Seth Bernard, May Erlewine and Seth Bernard brought earnest Michigan folk to Pickathon in 2009 and returned in 2010. They have since gone separate musical ways in the Midwest. Erlewine released What It Takes in 2025 and Receipts in August 2026.

intro: A Texas honky-tonk singer who holds to classic country.
story: Dale Watson, the Texas honky-tonk singer, held to classic country when he played Pickathon in 2009, with From the Cradle to the Grave among his records. He created the Ameripolitan Music Awards in 2014 and kept to the road. Unwanted, written and produced by Watson himself, came out on Forty Below Records on April 24, 2026.
sets: Sun Aug 2, 6:45 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 2, 11:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: An Asheville bluegrass band with soaring female harmonies.
story: Dehlia Low, an Asheville bluegrass quintet known for its female harmonies, played Pickathon in 2009. The band made two albums on Rebel Records and disbanded in the early 2010s, and co-founder Anya Hinkle has since built a solo career.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 6 pm, Woods Stage · Sat Aug 1, 5:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Philadelphia psych-pop band with Fate behind them.
story: Dr. Dog, the Philadelphia band of harmony-heavy psych-pop, played Pickathon in 2009 with Fate behind them and returned in 2010 and 2012. Shame, Shame arrived on Anti- in 2010 and Be the Void in 2012. They stepped back from full-time touring in 2021, returned with a self-titled album in 2024, and played select festivals in 2026.
sets: Sat Aug 1, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 1, 9:30 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: An old-time string band and Pickathon regulars.
story: Foghorn Stringband, a Portland old-time band, were Pickathon regulars by 2009, when they also anchored a square dance with caller Caroline Oakley. They became a cornerstone of the modern string-band revival and still tour, with Northeast dates including a show in Gray, Maine. Caleb Klauder and Reeb Willms keep up side projects.

intro: A California fiddler and banjoist with a 1920s sound.
story: Frank Fairfield, a California fiddler and banjoist, stunned Pickathon in 2009 with an old-time sound that might have come off a 1920s 78-rpm record. He came back in 2010 and again in 2022. He prefers acoustic intimacy to the spotlight and appears selectively, for special performances.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 2:30 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 12:45 pm, Fir Meadow Stage

intro: A Portland blues duo of slide guitar and buckets.
story: Hillstomp, the Portland duo of Henry Christian and John Johnson, turned buckets, washboards and slide guitar into junkbox blues, and had played Pickathon in 2004 before returning in 2009. More than two decades on, they staged a Last Hurrah show at The Belfry in Sisters, Oregon, in October 2025.

intro: A Portland chamber-folk band led by Justin Ringle.
story: Horse Feathers, the Portland chamber-folk band led by Justin Ringle, played Pickathon in 2009 with House with No Home out on Kill Rock Stars the year before. Thistled Spring followed in 2010 and Cynic's New Year in 2012, which Paste and PopMatters both praised. Kill Rock Stars announced a twentieth-anniversary vinyl reissue of the debut, Words Are Dead, for 2026.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 1:30 pm, Woods Stage · Sun Aug 2, late night (12:30 am), Starlight Stage · Sun Aug 2, 5 pm, Mountain View Stage

intro: A Portland bluegrass quartet with a honky-tonk edge.
story: Jackstraw, the Portland bluegrass quartet with a honky-tonk edge, were Pickathon fixtures by 2009, one of seven visits through 2022. They have stayed loyal to home, anchoring local stages and folk society gatherings, including a show for the Portland FolkMusic Society.

intro: A New York songwriter with Autumn Fallin' behind her.
story: Jaymay, the New York songwriter Jamie Seerman, played Pickathon in 2009 with her debut, Autumn Fallin', behind her, released on Heavenly in 2007. She went on to make independent records through 2016.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 5 pm, Workshop Barn · Sun Aug 2, 4 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 6 pm, Fir Meadow Stage · Sun Aug 2, 11:15 pm, Starlight Stage

intro: A former carpenter turned folk songwriter.
story: Joe Pug, a former carpenter with a harmonica rack and literate folk songs, played Pickathon in 2009. Messenger followed in 2010, the year the Americana Music Association nominated him for Emerging Act of the Year. Windfall came in 2015, and in 2025 he released Live at the Old Town School of Folk Music, while hosting his Working Songwriter podcast from Austin.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 4:30 pm, Fir Meadow Stage · Sat Aug 1, late night (1 am), Starlight Stage · Sat Aug 1, 4 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: An X co-founder at home in country and folk.
story: John Doe, co-founder of X and a pioneer of punk-country, played Pickathon in 2009 alongside The Sadies, the band he made the 2009 album Country Club with. Keeper followed in 2011, The Westerner in 2016 and Fables in a Foreign Land on Fat Possum in 2022. In summer 2026 his John Doe Folk Trio opened for Bob Dylan and Lucinda Williams.
sets: Fri Jul 31, 3:30 pm, Workshop Barn · Fri Jul 31, 8:45 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sat Aug 1, 10 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A young Nashville songwriter with Midnight at the Movies.
story: Justin Townes Earle played Pickathon in 2009 with Midnight at the Movies, on Bloodshot, his second album. That year the Americana Music Association named him Emerging Act of the Year, and the album and the artist were also nominated in other categories. Harlem River Blues followed in 2010, and its title song was named Song of the Year in 2011. He made eight albums, the last The Saint of Lost Causes in 2019, and died in 2020 at 38. An authorized biography, What Do You Do When You're Lonesome, was published in early 2026.

intro: A Georgia banjo picker with a high-octane sound.
story: Georgia banjo picker Larry Gillis brought his high-octane "swampgrass" sound to Pickathon in 2009 with the Larry Gillis Band, after decades on the traditional bluegrass festival circuit.
sets: Sat Aug 1, 11 am, Mountain View Stage · Sun Aug 2, 1 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 2, 3:30 pm, Workshop Barn

intro: A quiet standout of Portland's folk scene.
story: Laura Gibson played Pickathon in 2009 with Beasts of Season on Souterrain Transmissions, and returned in 2012. La Grande followed that year on Barsuk, and PopMatters and Pitchfork both reviewed it warmly. Empire Builder came in 2016 and Goners in 2018, and she earned an MFA in fiction. In late 2026 she signed with Loose Music and released the single "Sylvia."
sets: Fri Jul 31, 5:15 pm, Mountain View Stage · Sat Aug 1, 12 pm, Woods Stage

intro: A punk-spirited Cajun band from Louisiana.
story: Lost Bayou Ramblers, the Louisiana Cajun band of brothers Andre and Louis Michot, played Pickathon in 2009 with Live: Á la Blue Moon behind them, a 2008 Grammy nominee for Best Zydeco or Cajun Music Album. They returned in 2012 and 2018. Kalenda won the 2018 Grammy for Best Regional Roots Music Album, and Live: Orpheum Theater NOLA, recorded with the Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra, won the category again in 2024.

intro: A mandolin and flatpicked-guitar duo.
story: Mandolinist Mike Compton and flatpicking guitarist David Grier played Pickathon in 2009 as a duo, each a respected name in acoustic bluegrass. Both still perform, and David Grier was on the road with solo acoustic guitar dates in fall 2026 alongside his duo work with Compton.

story: Paleface, an anti-folk songwriter from New York's late-1980s scene, played Pickathon in 2009, after a visit in 2008. He went on to tour full-time as a duo with drummer Monica "Mo" Samalot.

story: Between his work in The Everybodyfields and his solo career, Sam Quinn brought the indie-folk project Japan Ten to Pickathon in 2009 and returned in 2010. He released the cassette To the Feet of the Gods in 2010 and now performs mainly with The Cartwright Brothers in Tennessee.

intro: An Oklahoma songwriter of Choctaw heritage.
story: Samantha Crain, an Oklahoma singer-songwriter of Choctaw heritage, played Pickathon in 2009 with her band The Midnight Shivers and Songs in the Night out that spring. That fall she won Native American Music Awards for Folk Album of the Year and Songwriter of the Year, and in 2022 for Single of the Year. Her seventh album, Gumshoe, came out on Real Kind Records in 2025.

act: Thao & The Get Down Stay Down
intro: A San Francisco band just breaking out.

Know Better Learn Faster followed that year, and they returned in 2011 and 2016. The band has since wound down, and Thao Nguyen returned to Kill Rock Stars with her first new music in six years and toured with Lord Huron.

story: The Deep Dark Woods, a Canadian roots band led by Ryan Boldt, played Pickathon in 2009 with Winter Hours out that year, and returned in 2010. The Place I Left Behind in 2011 won a 2012 Canadian Folk Music Award for Contemporary Album of the Year and a Juno nomination, and Jubilee earned another. The Circle Remains came out in October 2025, followed by the single "East of the Sun."

story: The Sadies, Toronto's psychedelic country road warriors, were already well traveled when they played Pickathon in 2009, the year they made Country Club with John Doe, who played that weekend too. Darker Circles made the 2010 Polaris Prize shortlist, and And the Conquering Sun with Gord Downie followed in 2014. Guitarist Dallas Good died in February 2022 at 48, and Colder Streams, finished before his death, came out that July. The band keeps touring North America and Europe.

story: Town Mountain, a hard-driving Asheville bluegrass band formed in 2005, played Pickathon in 2009 and returned in 2010, 2016 and 2019. Leave the Bottle came out in 2012, and in 2013 the IBMA named them Momentum Band of the Year, with singer Robert Greer taking Vocalist of the Year. They went on to widen into outlaw country and Americana.
